payload.headline: Netflix breaks below old support; still waiting, first buy level now 60.37

summary.thesis: Netflix is a cash-rich business trading cheaply against its own history and its peers, but sales growth is slowing, estimates are being cut and margins sit at a peak, so the price has not found a floor yet.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait, then buy at 60.37 and add at 58.22. Swing: no trade while the downtrend lasts.
summary.act_at: buy at 60.37, add at 58.22, no buying above 64.3

payload.happening: Netflix fell 2.25% to close at 60.75. That is below the 61.14–61.64 zone, which the data now lists as resistance (a ceiling) rather than support (a floor), and no support level appears below the price. The only news is a confirmed Netflix animated series based on Magic: The Gathering. The next earnings report is on 2027-01-19.
payload.business: The business itself is still strong. Revenue over the last twelve months was 49.7B, up from 43.4B. Free cash flow, the cash left after running and investing in the business, rose to 11.4B from 9.0B. Operating margin, the share of sales kept as operating profit, improved to 31.3% from 29.14%. The share count fell 3.35% in a year, so each share owns a bit more of the company. What is at risk is the pace. Quarterly sales growth slowed to 11.85% from 16.19% two quarters earlier. Analysts cut their estimate for this quarter's earnings per share by 7.3% in 30 days, to 0.68. The filings also say the 31% operating margin sits at the top of its 5-year range of 17–31%, and peaks like that usually fade. The balance sheet is not a pressing worry: debt of 12.7B against cash of 8.2B leaves net debt of 4.4B, which is small next to 11.4B of yearly free cash flow. The animated-series news is about content and mood. It does not change demand, margins or cash in any way the data can show. Segment data is not available.

worth.text: At 60.75, the discounted cash flow model (a DCF, which values today's estimate of all future cash) says the market expects free cash flow to start growing at about 13.7% a year, using a 10.1% discount rate. If starting growth is 10%, the value is 52.3. If it is 20%, the value is 77.98. The model's middle case is 64.3, with a bear case of 37.83 and a bull case of 76.88. Measured against its own history, the stock looks much cheaper. Its price-to-sales ratio of 5.0 sits at the 23rd percentile of its own 5-year range and below the peer median of 7.3, which puts the own-history value between 60.37 and 122.15, with a midpoint of 84.5. The gap between the two methods comes down to one question: does Netflix still deserve the multiples it earned when it grew faster? The earnings multiples are modest, at 17.3 times trailing earnings and 16.1 times next year's. Margin is the main thing that could pull the value down: if operating margin fell to 23%, the value would be 58.22, and at 15% it would be 38.45.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow starts growing somewhere between 10% and 20% a year, close to the 13.7% the price implies, even though quarterly sales growth has slowed to 11.85%.

bull: Cheap against peers and its own past: price-to-sales of 5.0 against a peer median of 7.3, and at the 23rd percentile of its own 5-year range.
Cash generation is rising: free cash flow grew to 11.4B from 9.0B, a 22.87% free cash flow margin.
Shareholders own more each year: the share count fell 3.35% in a year, and operating margin rose to 31.3% from 29.14%.
bear: Growth is slowing: quarterly sales growth fell to 11.85% from 16.19% two quarters ago.
Estimates keep falling: this quarter's earnings-per-share estimate was cut 7.3% in 30 days, to 0.68.
The margin is at a 5-year peak of 31%. A fade to 23% would put value at 58.22, below today's 60.75.

levels.what: Low end of the own-history price-to-sales range, next to the 60 put strike with the most open interest (38265). This is where to start a first, small position.
Value if operating margin fades to 23%. Buying here means the margin-peak risk is already paid for, so this is where to add.
DCF base value. Above it the margin of safety is gone, so no buying there.

longterm.why: The business is grade B and cheap on most measures. But the old floor broke, no support appears below the price, and estimates are still being cut. The plan is to buy lower, at prices that already allow for some margin fade.

swing.why: The trend is down: lower highs and lower lows, below the falling 20-, 50- and 200-day averages (63.88, 68.83, 80.38), and no support level is listed below 60.75. There is no trade until the stock closes above the 20-day average of 63.88 and the 64.56–65.08 resistance.

decision.timing: The 2027-01-19 report comes after the 2027-01-15 option expiry, and options price a move of about 11.7% by that date. With estimates still falling, any buying before the report should stay small and stay at 60.37 or below.

change_mind: A close above 65.08, the top of resistance, with the price back above the 20-day average of 63.88, would end the downtrend case and reopen a swing entry.
If the next-quarter earnings-per-share estimate climbs back from 0.92 to its 30-day-ago level of 0.94, the cuts have stopped, and buying could start nearer 60.75.

If the 2027-01-19 report shows quarterly sales growth below 11.85% together with operating margin falling from 31.3%, the fair-value range moves toward its 52.3 low and the 58.22 add level would be too high.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait, but the first buy level moves down from 61.63 to 60.37 because the stock closed at 60.75, below the old support zone that now shows as resistance at 61.14–61.64.
